correctness.rationale: Under the stated distinct-third-edge rule, a selected three-edge path is impossible (its middle edge is a forbidden third edge), as is a selected triangle. Hence the selected-edge components are stars; three leaves cannot all be independent within the allowed offsets −2,−1,1,2. The two-leaf offsets (−2,1),(−1,2),(−2,2) give two width-four and one width-five patterns. The nearest-endpoint and interleaving arguments force an exact two-unused-vertex minimum gap between spans; the gap and leaf conditions also suffice. Unique ordered components then give T^t x^{2(t−1)}/(1−x)^{t+1}, and leftover vertices distributed in t+1 slots give the binomial expression, including the constant 1. For m>0 selected edges the minimum order is 3m−2 plus the parity of m, attained with the shortest tiles. For n=6k+r and r=0,1, the only maximal families have 0 or 2 singleton tiles. After dividing out 2^k, their slack counts are [y^(r+2)](1+y/2)^k/(1−y)^(k+1) and binom(k+1,2)/2 times [y^r](1+y)^2(1+y/2)^(k−1)/(1−y)^(k+2). Expanding at r=0,1 gives the claimed numerators 11k²+17k+8 (over 8) and 15k³+47k²+50k+16 (over 16). Residues 2,3 have one singleton and slack 0,1; residues 4,5 have no singletons and slack 0,1. A slack unit either lengthens a tile or is placed in one gap, yielding the other four formulas. I separately enumerated every edge subset up to n=11 by conflict masks directly on graph edges and compared complete coefficients, and checked the exact rational/integer maxima through 50 using the rational GF's recurrence. Order zero gives 1 as intended; orders 1–5 give the stated maxima multiplicities. No finite test substitutes for the structural proof.

value.rationale: The gap-and-tile description isolates the local mechanism of the packing on a basic infinite chordal graph family and gives every subset-size coefficient, not only the optimum. The exact residue-dependent multiplicity exposes how width slack and alternative singleton tiles create many optima at certain lengths, information not provided by scalar optimization.
